sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Polyresin Vacuum Casting and Hand-Painted Limited Edition Statues

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national legal system with administrative-law overlay)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (amended 2010)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 through L.561-50-1 and R.561-1 through R.561-62; Ordonnance n° 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 (4th AML Directive); Décret n° 2017-1094 of 14 June 2017 (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs – RBE); Loi n° 2020-1508 of 3 December 2020 (5th AML Directive); EU Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 on funds transfers.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Fully_Public (exact residential address redacted; underlying source documents restricted to authorities and regulated professional access under CMF Article L.561-2-2-II)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each proposed gérant and each beneficial owner (notarized and apostilled)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notarial or consular authority in the country of residence of the signatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal record (equivalent to the French casier judiciaire) for the proposed gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal records authority of the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (bank statement or utility bill) of each founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution or utility provider of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (where origin country is not party to the Hague Convention) or notarized certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, current statutes, and certificate of good standing of any proposed foreign corporate shareholder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory two-layer screening applied at onboarding, on any change of control, and on a continuous automated basis: (1) EU consolidated financial sanctions list and UN Security Council consolidated list; (2) OFAC SDN and 50% rule as a prudent market standard; (3) PEP, family members, and close associates screening per FATF Recommendation 12 and EBA/ACPR Guidelines; (4) French Direction générale du Trésor and ACPR formalities; (5) verification of each identified UBO holding more than 25% with documented evidence chain pursuant to CMF Articles L.561-2-2 and R.561-1.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprise operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); name availability verified against the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS/RCS) through data.inpi.fr and infogreffe.fr.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Latin characters and recorded by the RCS in the French character set; foreign-language or Latin-script transliterated names are admissible provided they are written in the statuts, do not contravene public order or bonos mores, and are not misleadingly identical or confusingly similar to existing RCS entries, protected corporate names, or registered trademarks; Law n° 94-665 (Toubon) governs the mandatory French language use in commercial documentation, not the legal name itself.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Chapter III - Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL formation and management); Articles R.223-1 to R.223-33 (registration procedure); Order No. 2022-1443 and Decree No. 2023-430 on the Guichet Unique Electronique.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) kept by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, filed exclusively through the Guichet Unique Electronique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (Articles of Association) accompanied by the M0 creation declaration (Déclaration de création de société) and the supporting dossiers referenced in Article R.123-101 of the Commercial Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum for SARL; capital is freely set in the Articles of Association. Cash contributions (apports en numéraire) must be fully subscribed and paid up as to at least 20% at incorporation, with the balance payable within five years. Undisbursed funds must be deposited into a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and released only upon presentation of the RCS K-bis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE SHAREHOLDERS OF [COMPANY] SARL Unanimously: 1. The subscription of [X] shares at €[Y] each is ratified, forming the fully subscribed share capital of €[Z]; at least twenty percent of cash contributions has been paid up in accordance with Article L.223-7 of the Commercial Code. 2. The registered office is fixed at [address], France, within the jurisdiction of the local Commercial Court Registry. 3. [Name] is appointed Gérant (Manager) for an indefinite term, with the broadest powers to manage the company and complete all incorporation formalities. 4. The Gérant is authorized to publish the statutory announcement and to file the entire creation dossier with the Guichet Unique, obtaining the K-bis extract upon completion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Block Share Capital and Obtain Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (direct or via notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked current account (compte bloqué) in the name of the SARL in formation. Transfer the subscribed cash contributions (recommended 100% paid-up to simplify closure) and request a certificate of deposit (certificat de dépôt des fonds / attestation de blocage) stating the company name, the depositor, the amount and the account number. The certificate is valid until registration and must be handed to the notary or attached to the M0 file.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (statuts)
Identity documents of each subscribing shareholder
Bank account opening form and AML/KYC questionnaire
Proof of credit of the share capital (wire confirmation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses opening or blocking, apply to a second credit institution; if the certificate contains errors in names, amounts or account references, require a corrected certificate before filing to avoid a registry query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the Statutory Legal Notice (Avis de Constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and submit the incorporation notice containing the corporate name, legal form (SARL), share capital, registered office, corporate purpose (design, vacuum casting, painting and sale of polyresin statues and garage kits), term and identity of the Gérant. Obtain the attestation de parution (proof of publication) and retain it for the M0 dossier.
required_dossiers: Text of the avis de constitution approved by the shareholders
Attestation de parution issued by the JAL after publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any misprint must be corrected by a rectifying second insertion (insertion rectificative) within one month of the original publication, at the cost of the party responsible; the corrected attestation must be filed with the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Compile the Complete Creation File (M0) on the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Guichet Unique, create the applicant account, select 'création de personne morale' and complete the electronic M0 declaration: corporate details, registered office, managers, share capital, beneficial owner declaration (bénéficiaires effectifs), intended activity code (APE 32.40Z) and legal announcement reference. Upload the statutory documents in PDF/A format and verify the file completeness before electronic signature.
required_dossiers: Signed statuts, each page initialed
Certificat de dépôt des fonds (bank blocking certificate)
Attestation de parution of the legal notice
Déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs (form DBE)
Passports or national ID cards of shareholders and manager
Sworn statement of non-conviction of the manager
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
Second proof of address of the registered office (lease or ownership title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique issues a request for additional documents (demande de pièces complémentaires), respond within 15 days through the portal; failure to respond causes the file to lapse and requires a fresh submission with new fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay Fees, Submit, and Obtain RCS Registration (K-bis Extract)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, via the Guichet Unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic file, pay the official registry fee of approximately €84, and await the greffe's legality check. Upon approval, the company is registered at the RCS, INSEE attributes the SIREN/SIRET identifiers, and the immatriculation certificate (extrait K-bis) is made available on the portal. This K-bis confers full legal personality on the SARL.
required_dossiers: Complete validated M0 file
Guichet Unique payment confirmation
Receipt of the K-bis extract from the portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is refused, the greffe must state written reasons; the applicant may cure the deficiencies by resubmission within 15 days or contest the refusal before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce by means of a référé procedure within one month of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activate Tax, Social, Customs and Bank Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGFiP (Service des Impôts des Entreprises), URSSAF, INSEE and the definitive French bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: With the K-bis extract, open the definitive corporate bank account, then provide the RIB to the original depositary bank to release the blocked capital. The Guichet Unique automatically transmits data to DGFiP for VAT (TVA), corporate income tax (IS) and the EORI number; verify the SIE notifications and, if hiring staff, complete the employer registration for payroll declarations via URSSAF. Verify the APE code 32.40Z and update the company profile as needed.
required_dossiers: Extrait K-bis
Final corporate bank account RIB
EORI number confirmation (intra-EU trade)
SIRET notice from INSEE
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social identifiers are not received within 10 days, escalate to the INPI support desk; any error in the K-bis (address, name, activity code) is corrected through a free request for rectification (demande de rectification) addressed to the greffe.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREETS (Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités) for labour and workplace compliance; DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement) for installations classées and environmental permitting.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — manufacture of polyresin statues and garage kits is not a regulated profession under French law. The atelier qualifies as a non-classified ICPE (Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement) provided annual resin throughput remains below 100 tonnes and workshop floor area below 2,000 m², so no prefectural operating permit or declaration is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL — Inspection des Installations Classées, on behalf of the Ministry of Ecological Transition
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (non classée) — the activity does not appear in the Annex to Article R.122-2 of the Environment Code for projects subject to systematic or case-by-case EIA; a notice of non-classification is issued by DREAL on simple request for bank and insurer purposes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to municipal sewer per the Code of Public Health and the local sanitation regulation: pH 5.5–8.5, temperature ≤ 30°C, suspended solids ≤ 600 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 800 mg/L, no free styrene or untreated solvent discharge. Atmospheric VOC: apply best available techniques under Directive 2010/75/EU, keeping solvent consumption below 15 t/year (below Chapter V screening threshold); occupational styrene exposure limits per Articles R.4412-149 and R.4412-150 of the Labour Code: 8-hour VLEP 50 ppm, 15-minute VLCT 100 ppm. Hazardous waste (resin residues, acetone, contaminated rags) must be disposed through approved centers with waste tracking slips (bordereaux de suivi des déchets).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: 5th-category establishment notice to the mayor, evacuation signage, registered fire extinguishers and an annual fire drill log; electrical installation inspected and certified by an approved body within the last five years; structural load verification of resin storage racks. Occupational clearance: mandatory DUERP (document unique d'évaluation des risques) covering chemical, manual handling and electrical hazards; medical fitness monitoring of workers exposed to styrene and VOC through the service de prévention et de santé au travail; first-aid training and a first-aid kit on site. Urban-planning clearance: verification that the workshop premises comply with the local Plan Local d'Urbanisme craft zone rules prior to lease signing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); online portal: impots.gouv.fr; non-resident VAT registration unit: Service des Impôts des Entreprises Non-Résidents (SIE Non-Résidents).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Form the French SARL through Guichet des Formalités (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) to obtain the SIREN identification number and the SIRET establishment number. 2) File for corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés) status with the competent SIE. 3) For VAT, use Form 1065 (Cerfa n° 15787) to register with the SIE; a non-established foreign company must register directly with SIE Non-Résidents before making taxable supplies in France, and a non-EU third-country supplier must appoint an accredited fiscal representative in France. An EU taxable person making intra-Community distance sales above EUR 10,000 must register for French VAT either through the OSS system or via SIE Non-Résidents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a SARL is a taxable company subject to French corporate income tax at a 25% standard rate on taxable profits; it is not fiscally transparent by default. Territorial scope: a resident SARL is taxable on profits derived from businesses operated in France, with profits attributable to a foreign permanent establishment generally sheltered under French territoriality. Non-resident companies are taxable only on French-source profits if they operate through a French permanent establishment. No Tax_Exempt_Zone treatment applies to this entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in the French system. France does not permit a unilateral hybrid-mismatch election. The only material transparency election for a SARL is Article 239 bis AA of the CGI, under which a family SARL whose shareholders are exclusively natural persons in the direct line, or siblings, may opt for taxation as a partnership (régime des sociétés de personnes) instead of corporate income tax. An EURL with a single individual shareholder is taxed at the shareholder's income-tax level unless it opts for corporate income tax. Hybrid entity outcomes are governed by France's ATAD transposition rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for non-established foreign suppliers; for an established French SARL selling goods, the franchise exemption applies until annual taxable turnover reaches EUR 85,000 (main threshold) or EUR 93,500 (marginal tolerance), after which full VAT registration is mandatory. For services the threshold is EUR 37,500 (EUR 41,000 tolerance). Intra-Community acquisitions of goods by a VAT-registered SARL also require monitoring above EUR 10,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates B2B electronic invoicing under the Facturation électronique reform applicable from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-sized enterprises and 1 September 2027 for smaller businesses. Invoices must be transmitted through a certified PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) using structured data APIs or through the public portal choral.finances.gouv.fr. There is no real-time fiscal stamping or pre-clearance of each individual invoice; instead, structured e-invoice data and e-reporting data are submitted electronically, and DGFiP performs digital audits. Export invoices must include all statutory French invoice mentions and supporting data retained for at least 6 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: VAT zero-rating applies to exports of resin statues outside the European Union where the seller proves that the goods were physically sent from French customs territory to a non-EU destination and the export customs declaration was accepted by French Customs. Intra-EU supplies of goods to a VAT-registered business in another Member State are exempt (not zero-rated) upon the buyer's valid EU VAT number, subject to Intrastat reporting. Incoterms must support transfer of risk to the foreign buyer. Input VAT directly attributable to export transactions may be recovered provided the export documentary file satisfies Articles 262-263 CGI.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Déclaration en détail via the DELTA/GUN system) formally accepted by French Customs and showing the non-EU destination
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical shipment from France to the non-EU consignee
Commercial invoice and packing list with Incoterms and value of the exported resin statues
Inward remittance certificate or bank payment evidence showing the export proceeds were actually received and repatriated to France
Export contract or purchase order linking the buyer, invoice, shipment, and payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French Customs and DGFiP require production of the complete export file on request. If export zero-rating is unsupported or if the invoice is considered materially false, the VAT not priced out is assessed at 20%, with statutory late-payment interest and penalties: a 50% surtax under Article 1729 CGI for deliberate misstatement or concealed operation, 80% for abusive behavior, fraud by use of false invoices, or opposition to tax control. The standard retroactive reassessment period is three calendar years, extended to ten years for fully concealed activities. Criminal prosecution for export VAT fraud can lead to fines up to EUR 1,000,000 and imprisonment of up to seven years. Export zero-rating may be retrospectively clawed back and penalty interest charged if foreign exchange repatriation is not completed within 180 days or documentation is incomplete.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and competent Commercial Court Registry (Greffe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must generally be approved within six months after financial year-end and filed within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction, civil fine generally up to EUR 1,500, potentially EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance, and possible ex officio administrative radiation after formal notice and continued failure; no single automatic strike-off deadline applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and required schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within three months after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, normally by the second business day after 1 May, subject to the annually published electronic filing calendar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month and a 10% late-filing or late-payment surcharge, increasing in cases involving formal notice, concealment, or fraudulent conduct.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders meeting for approval of accounts and allocation of profit or loss
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SARL shareholders; minutes retained in the company's statutory records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each financial year, unless an extension is granted by the competent court.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Possible court order compelling approval, director liability for resulting loss, and penalties connected with failure to file approved annual accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information review and update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Beneficial Ownership Register administered through the competent Commercial Court Registry or the designated business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate annual confirmation filing is required solely because a year has elapsed; amendments must generally be filed within 30 days after the relevant change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice, court injunction, criminal penalties for inaccurate or missing beneficial ownership information, and possible restrictions or administrative measures affecting the company's registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounting and corporate register audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; reviewed by the statutory auditor where an auditor is appointed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least annually before account approval and whenever required to prepare the annual accounts or support statutory filings.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No standalone government filing penalty; deficiencies may create director liability, evidentiary risks, accounting sanctions, or statutory auditor reporting consequences.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SARL generally must appoint a statutory auditor when it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at the relevant closing date: EUR 5 million total balance sheet assets, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Appointment may also be required for qualifying groups or by court order, and may be made voluntarily.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Standalone SARL financial statements generally follow French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) regulations. IFRS is not generally mandatory for an unlisted SARL's standalone accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company should review its ownership chain, control structure, directors, share transfers, and beneficial ownership data at least annually. France does not require a separate annual no-change UBO confirmation; a corrected filing is required within 30 days after any reportable change. Share transfers must be documented, recorded in the company's share-transfer and shareholder records, and reflected in the UBO filing where control or beneficial ownership changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share transfers and shareholder accounts
Register of Directors and company officers
Minute Book and register of shareholder decisions
Annual accounts, management reports, and supporting corporate approvals

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 600-1,800 per year for a standard French registered-office or domiciliation service, excluding premium address and mail-forwarding services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-10,000 per year for a small SARL requiring a statutory audit; no statutory audit fee applies where the company is below mandatory thresholds and has not appointed an auditor.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit per 12-month period, with the balance taxed at 25%. Conditions generally include annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, capital fully paid up, and at least 75% of capital held by individuals or qualifying companies meeting the ownership condition. The 15% rate is not automatic; the company must meet the statutory conditions. Other incentives may apply to qualifying research, innovation, or geographic activities, but none is established by the stated resin-statue business scope.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward, subject to an annual deduction ceiling of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. The portion not deductible under the ceiling carries forward. A loss carryback may generally be elected for the preceding fiscal year, limited to EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), with the applicable detailed tax and financial statements: forms 2050-SD to 2059-G-SD under the normal regime, or forms 2033-A-SD to 2033-G-SD under the simplified regime. Submit electronically through the French tax administration's professional online account using EDI-TDFC or, where available, the relevant online filing service. A SARL is generally subject to IS unless a valid statutory election for income-tax treatment applies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return. IS instalments are generally paid quarterly; a company may be exempt from instalments where the preceding year's IS liability does not exceed EUR 3,000. The annual balance is paid separately.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the statutory date is the second working day following 1 May; the tax administration generally allows an additional 15 calendar days for electronic filing. Pay the IS balance by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end; for a 31 December year-end, generally 15 May. Quarterly instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December for a calendar-year company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the company's legal name, SIREN, address, fiscal year dates, tax regime, and contact details; identify the applicable normal or simplified tax package.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned French SARL files as a French tax-resident company on its French taxable results. Identify the French SARL, not its foreign shareholder, as the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable profit or loss and applicable IS computation, including any eligible reduced-rate portion, credits, and balance due, consistent with the attached tax statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the SARL's French taxable income and statutory adjustments. Do not include a foreign shareholder's income merely because it owns the SARL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide the balance sheet, profit and loss account, fixed-asset and depreciation details, provisions, tax adjustments, and related schedules required by the applicable accounting regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French entity's books and tax adjustments. Disclose cross-border related-party transactions in the relevant schedules and supporting filings where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pay each applicable quarterly instalment based on the prior year's tax liability or the prescribed current-year estimate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not replace the SARL as payer. The French SARL remains responsible for its instalments and payment references.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report and pay the annual IS balance after crediting instalments and eligible tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay through the SARL's French professional tax account; foreign ownership does not defer the statutory payment deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, rising to 40% if the return remains unfiled 30 days after formal notice, and potentially 80% for specified serious misconduct. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge plus late-payment interest, currently 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules and exceptions. Understatements may attract penalties of 10%, 40%, or 80%, depending on conduct and circumstances. The administration may assess tax by estimation or ex officio where filing obligations are not met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2257-SD, annual transfer-pricing summary declaration, filed electronically through the French professional tax portal when the statutory conditions apply. Companies subject to the full transfer-pricing documentation requirement generally provide the documentation under the applicable audit procedure rather than filing it as an attachment to the annual IS return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual where the filing threshold and scope conditions are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due within six months after the deadline for filing the annual corporate income tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the French reporting company, its group, and relevant foreign related entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the French SARL as the reporting entity where it meets the statutory conditions; disclose relevant foreign group entities and transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summarize relevant cross-border transactions with associated enterprises by transaction category and amount, including applicable pricing-policy information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include cross-border purchases, sales, services, royalties, financing, and other reportable related-party dealings; reconcile amounts to accounting records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or incomplete filing may result in a fine generally up to EUR 150, with an increased amount for omissions or inaccuracies, and may increase audit exposure. Failure to provide mandatory transfer-pricing documentation on request can trigger a penalty generally equal to the greater of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of the transactions covered by missing documentation, subject to a statutory minimum and maximum and the applicable procedural rules.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate shareholder are generally subject to 25% withholding tax, subject to treaty relief and statutory exemptions. A qualifying EU parent may be exempt under the Parent-Subsidiary regime, generally requiring a qualifying holding of at least 10% for at least two years, subject to anti-abuse and other conditions. Different domestic rules apply to individual recipients; the recipient's legal status must be verified.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Determine the recipient's treaty residence, beneficial ownership, legal form, holding, and eligibility under the relevant bilateral tax treaty or EU directive. Obtain a certificate of tax residence from the competent foreign tax authority and submit the applicable French treaty forms to the French payer before payment where possible. Form 5000 is commonly used to certify residence; the relevant payment-specific form may include Form 5001 for dividends, Form 5002 for interest, or Form 5003 for royalties, subject to treaty and current administrative procedures. If relief was not applied at source, the recipient may generally seek a refund using the applicable certified forms and supporting evidence. Treaty rates vary by treaty, recipient status, ownership, and beneficial-ownership conditions; no single treaty rate can be stated without the recipient's jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on royalties paid to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to treaty reduction, EU rules, and statutory exceptions; a 75% rate may apply to certain payments to jurisdictions or recipients covered by non-cooperative-jurisdiction provisions. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax, subject to statutory exceptions, anti-abuse provisions, and special rules including certain non-cooperative-jurisdiction payments. Treaty rates depend on the recipient's residence and the applicable treaty. EU Interest and Royalties Directive relief may be available for qualifying associated companies, subject to conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and Master File documentation generally applies to French entities or French permanent establishments whose annual turnover or gross assets are at least EUR 400 million, and to specified entities in groups meeting the statutory ownership or control conditions where a qualifying group entity reaches that threshold. A separate annual summary declaration, Form 2257-SD, generally applies at a lower threshold of EUR 50 million in annual turnover or gross assets, subject to statutory group and control conditions. Related-party transactions must in all cases comply with the arm's-length principle, and the tax administration may require supporting evidence.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a general Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to certain offshore regimes. French tax law nevertheless applies transfer-pricing rules, anti-abuse and sham-transaction doctrines, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled-foreign-company rules, and substance-based analysis in relevant contexts. A French SARL should maintain decision-making capacity, personnel or outsourced operational resources appropriate to its activities, accurate accounts, commercial evidence, and support for its pricing and financing arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing sales, falsifying invoices or accounts, claiming fictitious deductions, or using sham transactions to reduce IS or VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, interest, and penalties that may reach 80% in specified cases. Criminal tax fraud may result in up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine; aggravated cases may carry up to seven years' imprisonment and a EUR 3 million fine, subject to statutory conditions and possible higher proportional penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may face personal criminal liability where they personally participate in, direct, or knowingly facilitate fraud. Civil liability or recovery against a manager may arise under specific statutory conditions, including serious and repeated tax breaches. Imprisonment and travel restrictions are not automatic consequences of ordinary tax non-compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party sales, services, royalties, or financing outside the arm's-length range; failing to substantiate the commercial rationale; or failing to produce required documentation or declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may adjust taxable profit, impose interest and applicable tax penalties, and apply documentation-related fines, including the statutory minimum or transaction-based penalty where required documentation is not produced.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be exposed to civil or criminal liability where their own conduct constitutes fraud, falsification, or a separately sanctionable breach. An ordinary transfer-pricing adjustment does not automatically pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared or improperly relieved outbound withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends or royalties without withholding where required, applying a treaty rate without valid residence and eligibility evidence, or claiming an EU exemption without satisfying its conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French payer may be assessed for unpaid withholding tax, interest, and applicable penalties. Treaty or directive relief may be denied where beneficial ownership, anti-abuse, holding, or documentation requirements are not met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company-level liability is primary. Personal liability may arise only under specific statutory conditions or where a director knowingly participates in fraud or other unlawful conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an entity or contractual structure without genuine commercial purpose to obtain an improper tax advantage, conceal the beneficial recipient, or misstate the location of functions and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The administration may disregard the arrangement under applicable anti-abuse or sham-transaction rules, deny the tax benefit, reassess tax, and impose interest and enhanced penalties where statutory conditions are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal sanctions require a legal basis and facts establishing individual participation, fraud, or a specific statutory liability. Corporate status alone does not create automatic personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain reliable accounting records, issue compliant invoices, preserve supporting documents, or cooperate with a tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possible accounting adjustments, estimated assessments, denial of unsupported deductions, tax penalties, and separate accounting or commercial-law sanctions where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be personally liable for their own unlawful conduct or under specific statutory provisions. Civil, criminal, or travel restrictions are not automatic and require applicable legal grounds and procedures.
